entries.name: Agones
entries.use_for: Host and autoscale dedicated game servers on Kubernetes.
entries.why: CNCF-backed standard for running dedicated game servers on Kubernetes, originally from Google and Ubisoft.

entries.name: boardgame.io
entries.use_for: Build turn-based multiplayer games by writing just the game rules.
entries.why: Handles state, networking, turn order and AI bots for turn-based games; MIT.

entries.name: Colyseus
entries.use_for: Build authoritative multiplayer game servers in Node.js with automatic state sync.
entries.why: Popular Node.js multiplayer framework with room model and clients for JS, Unity, Defold, Haxe.

entries.name: GameNetworkingSockets
entries.use_for: Send reliable and unreliable encrypted messages over UDP in C++ games.
entries.why: Valve's Steam networking layer (~10k stars, BSD-3); fragmentation, encryption, P2P.

entries.name: KCP
entries.use_for: Get a fast reliable ARQ protocol over UDP with lower latency than TCP.
entries.why: Widely ported low-latency protocol (~17k stars, MIT) used in many online games.
entries.stable_reason: Small, complete ARQ protocol implementation in C; protocol is fixed and widely ported

entries.name: LiteNetLib
entries.use_for: Add lightweight reliable UDP networking to C#, Unity or Godot games.
entries.why: Popular C# reliable UDP library (~3.6k stars) used by many Unity netcode stacks.

entries.name: MagicOnion
entries.use_for: Build real-time game servers and RPC with shared C# interfaces over gRPC.
entries.why: Cysharp's C# RPC/real-time framework (~4.5k stars) for Unity and .NET servers.

entries.name: Matchbox
entries.use_for: Add peer-to-peer WebRTC networking to Rust and Bevy games, native and wasm.
entries.why: Rust WebRTC P2P networking (~1.2k stars) with signaling server; common with GGRS rollback.

entries.name: Mirror
entries.use_for: Add high-level multiplayer networking to Unity games.
entries.why: The most widely used open-source Unity networking library (MIT), with many transports.

entries.name: Nakama
entries.use_for: Run a game backend with accounts, realtime multiplayer, matchmaking, chat and leaderboards.
entries.why: Most complete open-source game backend, with client SDKs for Unity, Unreal, Godot and JS.

entries.name: netfox
entries.use_for: Add rollback netcode, time sync and interpolation to Godot multiplayer games.
entries.why: Leading Godot networking addon, with client-side prediction and lag compensation built in.

entries.name: Open Match
entries.use_for: Build custom matchmaking for multiplayer games on Kubernetes.
entries.why: Flexible matchmaking framework from Google that pairs with Agones; Apache-2.0 confirmed.

entries.name: PartyKit
entries.use_for: Build realtime multiplayer apps and games on edge rooms backed by Durable Objects.
entries.why: Simple room-based server model on Cloudflare; good fit for collaborative and casual multiplayer.

entries.name: Pitaya
entries.use_for: Build scalable, clustered game servers in Go with client SDKs.
entries.why: Production-proven at Wildlife Studios; built-in clustering, RPC and client libraries for iOS, Android, Unity.

entries.name: Quilkin
entries.use_for: Put a programmable UDP proxy in front of dedicated game servers.
entries.why: Built by Embark and Google for large-scale game traffic; adds security, routing and metrics.

entries.name: Riptide
entries.use_for: Add simple, lightweight message-based networking to C# and Unity games.
entries.why: Easy-to-use C# networking library (~1.3k stars, MIT) with Unity integration.

entries.name: Rivet
entries.use_for: Run stateful actors for multiplayer and realtime backends, self-hosted or managed.
entries.why: Open-source stateful actor platform (~6k stars, Apache-2.0) for realtime and game backends.

entries.name: yojimbo
entries.use_for: Build secure client/server networking for action games in C++.
entries.why: Glenn Fiedler's netcode library (~2.7k stars, BSD-3) for dedicated-server action games.
